guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, all three registers (prng_reseed_done_q, rnd_ctr_q, num_rounds_q) are cleared to zero at the next posedge of clk_i.
When rst_ni is high, each register updates to its corresponding D input (prng_reseed_done_d, rnd_ctr_d, num_rounds_d) at the next posedge of clk_i.

formal.consequent: prng_reseed_done_q == prng_reseed_done_d && rnd_ctr_q == rnd_ctr_d && num_rounds_q == num_rounds_d

formal_sketch.consequent: prng_reseed_done_q == prng_reseed_done_d && rnd_ctr_q == rnd_ctr_d && num_rounds_q == num_rounds_d

assumptions.claim: prng_reseed_done_d, rnd_ctr_d, num_rounds_d are driven to valid (non-X) logic values every cycle when rst_ni is high.
assumptions.risk: X-propagation or invalid states into the registered outputs can corrupt AES control (round count, PRNG seed status), leading to cryptographic malfunction or security weakness.

uncertain_points.claim: The reset value of num_rounds_q is 0. Is 0 a legal and safe number of AES rounds in the cipher control FSM? If the FSM starts using num_rounds_q before loading a valid round count, this could lead to zero-round encryption, bypassing cipher security.
uncertain_points.risk: Potential security vulnerability: zero-round operation may expose plaintext or use uninitialized key schedule, breaking confidentiality/integrity.

security_implications: The chunk resets prng_reseed_done_q, rnd_ctr_q, and num_rounds_q. A stale or zeroed num_rounds_q could cause the AES cipher to operate with zero rounds, effectively no encryption, exposing plaintext or weak key expansion. A zeroed prng_reseed_done_q may cause missing PRNG reseeds, weakening key/IV randomness. Both lead to integrity and confidentiality failures.
